description: Figure 1, titled “Distribution of Content Types in the DODa,” is a donut chart that visually represents the proportional breakdown of different content categories within the Darija Open Dataset. The chart is divided into six distinct colored segments, each corresponding to a specific content type as indicated by a legend positioned to the right: an orange segment for “Moroccan Names,” a dark purple segment for “Semantic Categories (e.g., Food, Economy),” a brown segment for “Syntactic Roles (e.g., Verbs, Nouns, Adjectives),” a yellow segment for “Translated Sentences,” a blue segment for “Extra + Augmented Data,” and a green segment for “Pending Translations.” Numerical values are displayed within each segment, indicating the count of entries for that category: “Syntactic Roles” has 23,108 entries, “Translated Sentences” has 45,387, “Pending Translations” has 43,000, “Extra + Augmented Data” has 30,000, “Semantic Categories” has 1,245, and “Moroccan Names” has 493. The chart does not include percentage labels inside the slices, but the relative sizes of the segments clearly show that “Translated Sentences” and “Pending Translations” are the largest components, followed by “Extra + Augmented Data,” while “Moroccan Names” and “Semantic Categories” represent the smallest portions. The chart is not exploded or otherwise visually emphasized, and the segments appear to be arranged in descending order of size, starting from the largest at the top right and moving clockwise.
